newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Shenzhen lists 100 firms in Jan-July.
newsitem.headline: China's Shenzhen lists 100 firms in Jan-July.

text.p: One hundred companies were listed on south China's Shenzhen Stock Exchange in the first seven months of this year, bringing the total on the bourse to 337, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Monday.
This compared with only 30 new listings in the year-ago period and 102 in all of 1996, the newspaper said.
China expanded its equities market from early 1997 to aid cash-strapped state enterprises and cool a stock market buying frenzy that had driven share prices sharply higher.

The 100 companies, most of them based in inland China and mainly involved in industrial production, issued a total of 5.194 billion shares and raised a combined 28.347 billion yuan, the newspaper said.

Of the newly listed firms, 54 have headquarters in central or western China, in line with the government's policy to boost the relatively backward economies of the nation's hinterland, it said, adding that this reverses the trend of mainly listing companies from coastal areas.
This helped to raise the proportion of inland-based firms listed in Shenzhen to 48.07 percent by the end of last month from 45.56 percent at end-1996, the newspaper said.
The 100 companies had relatively stronger earnings and larger share capital, it said.
The 1996 per-share net of the 100 companies averaged 0.489 yuan, higher than the entire Shenzhen bourse's average of 0.338 yuan, it said.
The total of outstanding shares of the 100 firms averaged 166 million each compared with an average of 101 million for the 102 firms listed in 1996.

Shenzhen's counterpart, the Shanghai bourse, lagged in the expansion competition, listing only 66 companies and raising proceeds of a total of 15.05 billion yuan in the first seven months, the newspaper said.
